narrative: Revenue is leaking through three specific categories, not the whole account: Power Tools, Consumables and Electrical Accessories each lost roughly half their monthly revenue since early 2026 and have not recovered. Overall revenue is down 34.5%, from ₹210,736 to ₹138,008 a month, with no seasonal precedent found. This is structural: declines are sustained 5-6 months with no bounce-back, while margin, discount and order pattern remain stable.
cited_evidence: Overall revenue fell 34.5%, from a baseline of ₹210,736 a month to a recent rate of ₹138,008 a month.
Power Tools revenue dropped 51%, from ₹48,822 to ₹23,921 a month, unrecovered for 6 months since February 2026.
Consumables fell 51.5%, from ₹27,363 to ₹13,265 a month, unrecovered for 5 months since April 2026.
Electrical Accessories declined 53.6%, from ₹24,398 to ₹11,325 a month, unrecovered for 5 months since April 2026.
No prior-year echo was found for any of these categories, and margin, discount and order pattern all stayed within normal swings.
recommended_actions: Contact the account to understand why Power Tools and Consumables orders dropped sharply since Q1 2026.
Check whether specific disappeared products (e.g. Cordless Drill 18V) reflect a switched supplier.
Track whether Precision Hardware's recovery pattern can be replicated in the other declining categories.

prioritization.reason: 24.7% of baseline monthly revenue at risk, medium confidence.

churn_risk_projection.basis: Assumes the current monthly loss rate persists unchanged for 12 months — not a forecast of further deterioration, just the cost of inaction at today's rate. Revenue and margin figures overlap and must not be added together.

model_agreement.agent_response: Model leans healthy on stable basket width and AOV, but three large categories show unrecovered 50%+ declines sustained 5-6 months, overriding that read.

evidence_timeline.headline: Discounting is stable
evidence_timeline.method: Creep threshold: 3.0pp. Discount is revenue-weighted, so a deep discount on a large line counts for more than the same discount on a small one.

evidence_timeline.method: Shift threshold: 8.0pp. Direction decides the verdict — the same size of move upward is premiumisation, not a downgrade.

breakdown.note: Lines share the account's expected months of continued buying, so their values add back to the account total. Line losses can exceed the account's value at risk because lines that grew offset part of the loss.

_lifetime_value.note: Lifetime value = value per month x the horizon months (12 or 24), flat. Expected orders and expected active months (BG/NBD, fitted on the whole book) are reported alongside for information and do not scale the money. Baseline uses the value per month before the recent window; current uses the recent window. Value at risk is the gap — the same loss the monthly figures show, on a longer clock. Never add it to monthly revenue at risk.
